name: momentum_ignition_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: When a stock breaks a multi-hour range (30+ bars) on a volume surge (> 3x average), stop-loss cascades from trapped range traders amplify the move for 10-30 bars. This is a microstructure phenomenon: range traders accumulate positions near the range boundaries, and their stops cluster just outside. The breakout triggers these stops, creating artificial but tradeable momentum. Edge persists because the stop cascade effect is structural to how leveraged intraday traders manage risk.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

indicators.name: bars_in_range
indicators.formula: count of consecutive bars where high < range_high_30 AND low > range_low_30
indicators.purpose: how long the range has held

filters.vix_filter: vix > 12 AND vix < 25 (need some vol for breakouts to work, but not chaos)
filters.volume_filter: vol_surge > 3.0 is the core entry condition
filters.expiry_filter: skip on expiry day (too much noise)

weaknesses: False breakouts are frequent — 55% of trades lose, requiring strong risk:reward to compensate
Slippage on breakout bars is higher than normal (4+ bps) due to momentum and competing algos
The 30-bar range lookback is somewhat arbitrary — different stocks consolidate on different timeframes
prior_art: Range breakout with volume confirmation — Toby Crabel, Linda Raschke, and countless others
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
